prompt.content:
You classify a user–assistant conversation.

Task 1 — Legal guidance: Is the USER seeking legal guidance or legal interpretation?
Answer <legal> with YES or NO. Focus on user intent.

Task 2 — Topic: If <legal> is YES, pick exactly one topic from the list below.
If <legal> is NO, write N/A for <topic>.

Legal guidance (YES) means the user wants legal interpretation, rights/obligations, or legal procedure for a real situation — similar to:
- "Can my landlord do this under Dutch law?"
- "What are my rights if I was fired without notice?"
- "Is this contract clause enforceable?"

Answer NO when the user is not seeking legal guidance (e.g. exam-style MCQs, pure summarization/translation of legal text, or tooling/dataset tasks) even if the text mentions law.

Topic list and descriptions:
Topics:
1) FAMILY: Marriage, divorce, child custody, child support, alimony, adoption, guardianship, domestic violence, parentage, family-status disputes.
2) HOUSING: Rent, eviction, landlord-tenant disputes, habitability, deposits, mortgages, foreclosure, neighbors, housing subsidies.
3) WORK: Employment contracts, wages, dismissal, discrimination at work, leave, workplace safety, severance, freelancers when the main issue is labor rights.
4) PUBLIC_BENEFITS: Unemployment benefits, disability, pensions, welfare, public assistance, eligibility, reductions, sanctions, appeals on benefits.
5) CRIMINAL_JUSTICE: Police, arrest, criminal charges, fines, prosecution, defense, victims' rights, probation, criminal procedure.
6) CONSUMER_DEBT: Purchases, warranties, subscriptions, refunds, scams, debt collection, loans, bankruptcy, credit, repossession, consumer finance.
7) CONTRACTS: Private civil agreements and breach/interpretation issues not better covered by work, housing, consumer, or business.
8) IMMIGRATION: Visas, residence permits, asylum, citizenship, deportation, family migration, immigration status and related procedures.
9) BUSINESS: Company formation, shareholder issues, commercial compliance, business operations, B2B disputes, self-employment when the main issue is business law.
10) DATA_PRIVACY: Personal data, surveillance, GDPR/privacy rights, data deletion, consent, monitoring, platform data practices.
11) INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY: Copyright, trademark, patent, trade secrets, licensing, infringement, ownership of creative or technical works.
12) CIVIL_RIGHTS: Discrimination outside employment/housing, free speech, due process, equal treatment, constitutional or human-rights style claims.
13) INTERNATIONAL_CROSS_BORDER: Choice of law, jurisdiction, treaty-based questions, cross-border enforcement, multi-country disputes where cross-border law is central.
14) OTHER: Genuinely legal but not covered above.

Topic rules:
- Use CONTRACTS only when the issue is mainly about a civil agreement and is not better captured by WORK, HOUSING, CONSUMER_DEBT, or BUSINESS.
- Use INTERNATIONAL_CROSS_BORDER only when the cross-border or jurisdictional aspect is central to the answer, not merely incidental.

─── EXACT VALUES — copy these strings verbatim, no other spelling is accepted ───
<legal> must be one of: YES, NO
<topic> must be one of: BUSINESS, CIVIL_RIGHTS, CONSUMER_DEBT, CONTRACTS, CRIMINAL_JUSTICE, DATA_PRIVACY, FAMILY, HOUSING, IMMIGRATION, INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY, INTERNATIONAL_CROSS_BORDER, OTHER, PUBLIC_BENEFITS, WORK, N/A

Important formatting rules:
• Use ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES for topic names — e.g. INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY, PUBLIC_BENEFITS, DATA_PRIVACY
• N/A uses a forward slash — not "NA", "N_A", or "n/a"
• DONT_KNOW uses an underscore — not "DONT KNOW", "Don't know", or "DontKnow"
• Topic names are case-insensitive when graded, but capitalisation matters for correctness — always use ALL CAPS
